slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 in a Pro plan at $12 more per seat, and plan on $2.9M of new ARR, not $8M
Copilot is worth launching, though its gains are smaller than claimed
–	Beta accounts scheduled 11% more jobs per dispatcher-hour, but they were volunteers
–	Routewise's AI puts at most $0.6M of our new ARR a year at stake
At $149, real buying points to about $2.5M of ARR, not the $8M proposed
–	Only 14% of beta accounts bought at $149, against 46% stated intent
–	Even $2.5M is a ceiling, because the beta accounts volunteered
A Pro plan at $12 more per seat is the better package, worth about $2.9M
–	A flat $149 draws heavy users: buyers cost $61 a month to serve
–	Pro prices with seats and matches Routewise's packaging
Pro meets both company targets and outweighs the mobile delay
–	Pro closes the NRR gap at 26% uptake, and the mobile delay risks at most $1.1M of ARR
Decide in January, sell Pro from Q2 2027 and restart the mobile rewrite in Q3
–	Guardrails: a fair-use allowance, a fixed mobile restart, a clean win-rate test, cheaper inference

A flat price sells to the accounts that cost most to serve
▪	Paywall buyers: sent 3.6 times the median account's requests, so inference takes 41% of the price
▪	Top 10%: inference alone reaches 88% of the price, before platform and support cost
▪	Median and mean accounts: cheap to serve, yet these are the accounts the $149 price failed to convert

The 2023 benchmark clears the bar; the volunteer paywall rate does not
▪	At the 33% uptake seen after the 2023 tier launch, Pro adds about 5.0 percentage points of NRR
▪	At the 14% paywall rate, Pro adds only 2.1 percentage points; win-backs or lower churn must close the rest
